source: W paired first attempt native AskUserQuestion calls, exact question/options/answers; no rescore of historical run

questions.question:
D1 — What does processPayment() return or raise when 502 retries are exhausted? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-failure-sig>

ELI10: When Stripe keeps returning 502 and the retry budget runs out (max_retries=1 means 2 total attempts), processPayment() has to signal failure to its caller. The 502 exhaustion test needs to assert this exact behavior — but the plan says only "fails clean" without defining what that means. Without a specified failure contract (exception class or error return), the test cannot be written correctly.

Stakes: An assumption here that's wrong means the test asserts the wrong contract — it may pass while not actually verifying the intended behavior, giving false confidence in a payment-critical path.

Recommendation: A because exception-raising is the most common payment failure pattern, most explicit for callers, and most directly testable.

Completeness: A=9/10, B=8/10, C=4/10

Net: A or B adds one sentence to the plan and unblocks implementation; C defers and creates ambiguity the implementer must resolve alone.

options.label: Specify: raises exception (Recommended)
options.description: Add to plan: "processPayment() raises PaymentError (or equivalent) on 502 exhaustion; no receipt is emitted." Implementer asserts the exception class in the 502 test.

options.label: Specify: returns error value
options.description: Add to plan: "processPayment() returns an error tuple/result on 502 exhaustion; no receipt is emitted." Implementer asserts the error return in the 502 test.

options.label: Defer to implementer
options.description: Leave failure contract unspecified. The developer reads the existing code to determine it at implementation time. Creates ambiguity; acceptable if the contract is already documented elsewhere.

questions.question:
D2 — What must the happy path test assert about the receipt? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-receipt-spec>

ELI10: The plan says "assert correct receipt is generated" but doesn't define what "correct" means. A receipt struct has multiple fields (amount, currency, customer_id, stripe_charge_id, etc.). The test could assert: (A) all key business fields by value, (B) only the Stripe-linked field (charge ID) to confirm the right charge was recorded, or (C) just that a receipt exists (smoke test only). Option A is a correctness test; C is a smoke test that would pass even with a half-populated receipt.

Stakes: A test that only checks receipt presence could pass while critical fields (amount, customer_id) are wrong — a payment is charged correctly in Stripe but the internal record is broken.

Recommendation: A because correctness means verifying the business-critical fields, not just existence. CC writes this in seconds.

Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10

Net: A vs C is the difference between a correctness test and a smoke test.

options.label: Full field assertion (Recommended)
options.description: Plan specifies: assert receipt.amount, receipt.currency, receipt.customer_id, and receipt.stripe_charge_id match expected values. Full structural correctness test.

options.label: Stripe linkage only
options.description: Plan specifies: assert receipt.stripe_charge_id matches the mock charge ID. Confirms the right charge was recorded; other fields assumed correct.

options.label: Presence only (smoke test)
options.description: Plan specifies: assert a receipt is returned (not nil/error). Minimal — does not verify field values.

questions.question:
D3–D6 — Which of these test quality additions should be added to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-test-quality>

ELI10: The plan's two tests are scoped correctly but leave 4 test quality gaps unspecified. Each is a one-liner to add to the plan and a few lines of test code. All are recommended — they separate a correctness test suite from a smoke test suite. With CC, implementation cost is negligible.

Recommendation: All four — each closes a real gap in what the test proves. Completeness: each is 10/10 with all selected, 7/10 without any.

Net: Selecting all turns the plan into a complete test specification; selecting none leaves implementation details to the developer's discretion.

options.label: Assert charge count (mock.call_count == 2)
options.description: 502 test must assert the Stripe mock was called exactly twice (one original + one retry). The factory exposes call history — the plan should require using it.

options.label: Assert backoff invoked (virtual_sleeper)
options.description: 502 test must assert the virtual sleeper was invoked (backoff actually fired, not skipped). The plan mentions the sleeper records backoff but doesn't require asserting it.

options.label: State test isolation explicitly
options.description: Plan should state: factory provides a fully mocked Stripe client; no real network calls. Prevents future confusion about whether these are true unit tests.

options.label: Require descriptive test names + messages
options.description: Plan should require descriptive test names and failure messages (e.g., 'expected 2 Stripe calls, got N'). Makes CI failures debuggable without reading the implementation.
